DEVICE PROTECTION PLAN TERMS
Issued by Voltguard Protection Ltd
In this policy, "the Provider" means Voltguard Protection Ltd and "the Customer" means the person named in the schedule.

§ 1  Definitions
(1) Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.
(2) Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.
(3) Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Provider, before any service fee, limit or sublimit is applied.
(4) Authorised repairer means a repairer approved in writing by the Provider.
(5) Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
(6) Breakdown means the failure of a part to work as the manufacturer intended, from an internal electrical or mechanical fault.
(7) Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
(8) Device means the item shown in the schedule, bought new from an authorised retailer.
(9) Family means the Customer's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Customer.
(10) Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
(11) Limit means the most the Provider will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
(12) Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 24 months after the device was bought.
(13) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Customer's schedule.
(14) Premium means the amount the Customer must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
(15) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(16) Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
(17) Replacement device means a device of the same or similar specification, which may be refurbished.
(18) Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Customer's details, the covers the Customer bought and any extensions.
(19) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
(20) Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

§ 2  Limits and service fee
(1) Accidental Damage: limit $800 per incident; service fee $79 per claim.
(2) Breakdown: limit $600 per incident; service fee $25 per claim.
(3) Theft and Loss: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
(4) The service fee is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

§ 3  Severability
(1) If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

§ 4  Assignment
(1) The Customer cannot transfer the Customer's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Provider's written consent.

§ 5  Communication
(1) The Provider will communicate with the Customer in English.
(2) The Provider may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

§ 6  Optional cover: Theft and Loss
(1) The Provider will replace the Customer's device if it is stolen or lost.
(2) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Customer's schedule.
(3) The most the Provider will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
(4) The Provider will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
(5) The Provider will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

§ 7  Subrogation
(1) The Provider will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Customer's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
(2) The Provider can take action in the Customer's name to recover any payment the Provider makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

§ 8  Change of address
(1) The Customer must tell the Provider within 30 days if the Customer changes the Customer's address.
(2) The Provider may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

§ 9  Arbitration
(1) If the Provider accepts a claim but disagree with the Customer about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
(2) Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against the Provider.

§ 10  Currency
(1) All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
(2) Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

§ 11  Breakdown
(1) The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
(2) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 45 days after the policy start date.
(3) The most the Provider will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $80 per incident.
(4) The Provider will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
(5) The Provider will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

§ 12  Joint policyholders
(1) Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
(2) A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

§ 13  Notices
(1) Any notice the Provider gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Provider holds.
(2) Notices from the Customer should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

§ 14  Compensation scheme
(1) The Provider is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
(2) If the Provider cannot meet the Provider's obligations, the Customer may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

§ 15  Changes in circumstances
(1) The Customer must tell the Provider as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
(2) The Provider may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

§ 16  Discounts
(1) Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
(2) If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Provider may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

§ 17  Software support
(1) The Provider's helpline can give advice on setting up and using the Customer's device.
(2) Software support does not include fixing problems caused by third-party apps or unofficial operating systems.

§ 18  Market conditions
(1) If the replacement item is no longer available, the Provider will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

§ 19  Renewal
(1) The Provider will write to the Customer at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
(2) The Provider is not obliged to offer renewal.

§ 20  Reasonable precautions
(1) The Customer must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
(2) The Customer must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

§ 21  Recovery of costs
(1) If the Provider pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Provider may ask the Customer to repay the amount.

§ 22  Duty of fair presentation
(1) The Customer must answer all questions the Provider asks honestly and to the best of the Customer's knowledge.
(2) If the Customer gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Provider may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
(3) If the Customer gives incorrect information carelessly, the Provider may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

§ 23  Salvage
(1) When the Provider replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Provider's property.
(2) If stolen property is recovered after the Provider has paid a claim, the Customer must tell the Provider and either return the payment or give the Provider the property.

§ 24  Environmental commitment
(1) Where practical, the Provider will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
(2) The Customer may ask for a new part instead, and the Provider will tell the Customer whether any additional cost would apply.

§ 25  Cooperation
(1) The Customer must give the Provider all the help and information the Provider reasonably need to settle a claim.
(2) The Customer must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Provider's written permission.

§ 26  Exchange of information
(1) To prevent fraud, the Provider may check the details the Customer gives against public records and industry databases.
(2) The Provider may contact previous insurers to confirm the Customer's claims history.

§ 27  Waiver
(1) If the Provider does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Provider has given up the right to enforce it later.

§ 28  Accessibility
(1) This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

§ 29  Accidental Damage
(1) The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it is accidentally damaged.
(2) The most the Provider will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
(3) The most the Provider will pay for Wearables under this section is $250 per incident.
(4) The Provider will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
(5) The Provider will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than the Provider or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if the Provider approved the repair in writing beforehand.

§ 30  Interest
(1) The Provider will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

§ 31  General exclusions
(1) The Provider will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(2) The Provider will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(3) The Provider will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
(4) The Provider will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Provider from paying.

§ 32  Fraud
(1) If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Provider will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
(2) The Provider may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

§ 33  Premium payment
(1) The Customer must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
(2) If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, the Provider may cancel the policy after giving notice.

§ 34  Third-party administrators
(1) The Provider may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Provider's behalf.
(2) Any company the Provider appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

§ 35  Data protection
(1) The Provider will use the personal information the Customer provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
(2) The Provider will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
(3) The Customer can ask for a copy of the personal information the Provider holds by writing to the Provider's data protection officer.

§ 36  Making a claim
(1) The Customer must notify the Provider of a claim within 30 days of the incident. The Provider will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(2) The Provider may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(3) The Customer must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

§ 37  Complaints
(1) If the Customer has a complaint, the Customer should first contact the Provider's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
(2) The Provider will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
(3) If the Customer remains dissatisfied, the Customer may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

§ 38  Instalment agreements
(1) If the Customer pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
(2) Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

§ 3  Reasonable precautions
(1) The Policyholder must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
(2) The Policyholder must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

(3) If the Policyholder remains dissatisfied, the Policyholder may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

(3) If the Policyholder gives incorrect information carelessly, the Insurer may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

(1) The Policyholder's contents are covered while temporarily removed from the home to another building in the same country, for up to 60 days.
(2) Contents in a student hall of residence are covered only if the student is a member of the Policyholder's family.

§ 21  Severability
(1) If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

§ 22  Market conditions
(1) If the replacement item is no longer available, the Insurer will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

§ 23  General exclusions
(1) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.
(2) The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(3) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(4) The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.

(1) Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.

(1) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

(1) The Policyholder cannot transfer the Policyholder's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Insurer's written consent.

(1) If the Policyholder rents the home, the Insurer will pay for damage to fixtures and fittings that the Policyholder installed and are responsible for.
(2) This cover applies only to improvements the Policyholder paid for, not to items provided by the landlord.

(1) Where practical, the Insurer will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.

§ 22  Instalment agreements

§ 23  Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)

§ 24  Recovery of costs

§ 25  Claims documents
(1) The Policyholder must provide, at the Policyholder's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Insurer reasonably ask for.

§ 26  Waiver
(1) If the Insurer does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Insurer has given up the right to enforce it later.

§ 27  Third-party administrators
(1) The Insurer may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Insurer's behalf.
(2) Any company the Insurer appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

§ 28  Locks and keys
(1) If the keys to the Policyholder's home are lost or stolen, the Insurer will pay the cost of replacing the locks to the outside doors.
(2) The most the Insurer will pay under this clause is $500 for any one claim.

ANNUAL MULTI-TRIP TRAVEL COVER
Issued by Bluewater Assurance
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Bluewater Assurance and "the Insured Person" means the person named in the schedule.

§ 1  Definitions
(1) Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
(2) Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
(3) Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 3,000 metres.
(4) Limit means the most the Insurer will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
(5) Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
(6) Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which the Insured Person received treatment or advice in the 6 months before the policy start date.
(7) Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 8 hours.
(8) Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
(9) Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
(10) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
(11) Territory means the countries in which cover applies, as shown in the schedule.
(12) Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with the Insured Person on the same trip.
(13) Trip means a journey that starts and ends in the Insured Person's home country during the policy period.
(14) Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

§ 2  Limits and excess
(1) Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(2) Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
(3) Trip Cancellation: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(4) Travel Delay: limit $300 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(5) The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

§ 3  Trip Cancellation
(1) The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
(2) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 14 days after the policy start date.
(3) The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
(4) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
(5) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

§ 4  Baggage and Personal Belongings
(1) The Insurer will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to the Insured Person's baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
(2) The most the Insurer will pay for Valuables under this section is $250 per incident.
(3) The most the Insurer will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.
(4) The Insurer will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
(5) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
(6) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

§ 5  Emergency Medical Expenses
(1) The Insurer will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
(2) The most the Insurer will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $400 per incident.
(3) The most the Insurer will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
(4) The Insurer will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
(5) The Insurer will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
(6) The Insurer will not pay for any claim arising from the Insured Person's being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

§ 6  Optional cover: Travel Delay
(1) The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
(2) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.
(3) The Insurer will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

§ 7  General exclusions
(1) The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
(2) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(3) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Insured Person.

§ 8  Making a claim
(1) The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 14 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(2) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(3) The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

§ 9  Exchange of information
(1) To prevent fraud, the Insurer may check the details the Insured Person gives against public records and industry databases.
(2) The Insurer may contact previous insurers to confirm the Insured Person's claims history.

§ 10  Records and evidence
(1) The Insured Person should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
(2) Where proof of value is missing, the Insurer may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
(3) The Insurer may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

§ 11  Changes in circumstances
(1) The Insured Person must tell the Insurer as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
(2) The Insurer may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

§ 12  Cooperation
(1) The Insured Person must give the Insurer all the help and information the Insurer reasonably need to settle a claim.
(2) The Insured Person must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Insurer's written permission.

§ 13  Fraud
(1) If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Insurer will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
(2) The Insurer may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

§ 14  Third-party administrators
(1) The Insurer may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Insurer's behalf.
(2) Any company the Insurer appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

§ 15  Complaints
(1) If the Insured Person has a complaint, the Insured Person should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
(2) The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
(3) If the Insured Person remains dissatisfied, the Insured Person may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

§ 16  Change of address
(1) The Insured Person must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Insured Person changes the Insured Person's address.
(2) The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

§ 17  Interest
(1) The Insurer will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

§ 18  Cancellation
(1) The Insured Person can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
(2) After the first 14 days the Insured Person can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
(3) The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Insured Person 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

§ 19  Rental car excess
(1) If the Insured Person hires a car during the trip, the Insurer will reimburse any excess the Insured Person must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
(2) This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

§ 20  Waiver
(1) If the Insurer does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Insurer has given up the right to enforce it later.

§ 21  Recovery of costs
(1) If the Insurer pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Insurer may ask the Insured Person to repay the amount.

§ 22  Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
(1) A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

§ 23  Notices
(1) Any notice the Insurer gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Insurer holds.
(2) Notices from the Insured Person should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

§ 24  Environmental commitment
(1) Where practical, the Insurer will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
(2) The Insured Person may ask for a new part instead, and the Insurer will tell the Insured Person whether any additional cost would apply.

§ 25  Market conditions
(1) If the replacement item is no longer available, the Insurer will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

§ 26  Communication
(1) The Insurer will communicate with the Insured Person in English.
(2) The Insurer may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

§ 27  Instalment agreements
(1) If the Insured Person pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
(2) Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

§ 28  Interpretation
(1) Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
(2) Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
(3) Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

§ 29  Discounts
(1) Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
(2) If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

§ 30  Data protection
(1) The Insurer will use the personal information the Insured Person provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
(2) The Insurer will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
(3) The Insured Person can ask for a copy of the personal information the Insurer holds by writing to the Insurer's data protection officer.

§ 31  Missed departure
(1) The Insurer will pay reasonable additional travel and accommodation costs to reach the Insured Person's destination if the Insured Person arrives too late to board the Insured Person's booked transport because public transport fails.
(2) The Insured Person must allow enough time to reach the departure point, and must obtain written confirmation of the delay from the transport operator.

§ 32  Automatic renewal
(1) Unless the Insured Person tells the Insurer otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Insurer holds.
(2) The Insured Person can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Insurer's helpline.

§ 33  Other insurance
(1) If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Insurer will pay only the Insurer's proportionate share.
(2) The Insured Person must tell the Insurer about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Insured Person makes a claim.

§ 34  Subrogation
(1) The Insurer will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Insured Person's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
(2) The Insurer can take action in the Insured Person's name to recover any payment the Insurer makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

§ 35  Taxes
(1) The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
(2) If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

§ 36  Joint policyholders
(1) Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
(2) A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

§ 37  Renewal
(1) The Insurer will write to the Insured Person at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
(2) The Insurer is not obliged to offer renewal.

§ 38  Duty of fair presentation
(1) The Insured Person must answer all questions the Insurer asks honestly and to the best of the Insured Person's knowledge.
(2) If the Insured Person gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Insurer may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
(3) If the Insured Person gives incorrect information carelessly, the Insurer may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

§ 39  Arbitration
(1) If the Insurer accepts a claim but disagree with the Insured Person about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
(2) Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against the Insurer.

§ 40  Salvage
(1) When the Insurer replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Insurer's property.
(2) If stolen property is recovered after the Insurer has paid a claim, the Insured Person must tell the Insurer and either return the payment or give the Insurer the property.

§ 41  Governing law
(1) This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
(2) Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

§ 42  Legal expenses abroad
(1) The Insurer will pay legal costs to pursue compensation for the Insured Person's injury or death caused by a third party during the trip.
(2) The Insurer will not pay legal costs unless the Insurer's legal adviser agrees that the claim has a reasonable prospect of success.

§ 43  Inflation
(1) The Insurer may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
(2) Any adjustment will be shown in the Insured Person's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

§ 44  Electronic documents
(1) The Insurer will send documents by email unless the Insured Person asks for paper copies.
(2) The Insured Person must tell the Insurer if the Insured Person's email address changes.
(3) Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

§ 45  Repatriation
(1) If the Insurer's medical adviser agrees it is necessary, the Insurer will arrange and pay for the Insured Person to be brought home.
(2) The Insurer will decide the method of transport and the time of repatriation after speaking to the treating doctor.

§ 46  Compensation scheme
(1) The Insurer is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
(2) If the Insurer cannot meet the Insurer's obligations, the Insured Person may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

§ 47  Personal liability
(1) The Insurer will pay damages the Insured Person becomes legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
(2) This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
(3) The most the Insurer will pay under this section is $1,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

§ 48  How to read this document
(1) This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
(2) Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
(3) Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

§ 49  Premium payment
(1) The Insured Person must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
(2) If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, the Insurer may cancel the policy after giving notice.

§ 50  Claims documents
(1) The Insured Person must provide, at the Insured Person's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Insurer reasonably ask for.
(2) The Insurer may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

§ 51  Accessibility
(1) This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

§ 52  Severability
(1) If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

§ 53  Assignment
(1) The Insured Person cannot transfer the Insured Person's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Insurer's written consent.

§ 54  Emergency assistance
(1) The Insurer's emergency assistance service is available 24 hours a day on the number shown in the schedule.
(2) The Insured Person must contact the assistance service before being admitted to hospital as an in-patient, unless it is an emergency.
(3) The assistance service can arrange payment guarantees, interpreters and transport home.

§ 55  Geographical limits
(1) Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
(2) Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

§ 56  Currency
(1) All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
(2) Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

§ 57  Reasonable precautions
(1) The Insured Person must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
(2) The Insured Person must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

§ 58  Payment of claims
(1) The Insurer will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Insured Person's name.
(2) The Insurer aims to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents the Insurer needs.

§ 59  Sanctions
(1) The Insurer will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Insurer to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

§ 60  Customer support
(1) The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
(2) Outside these hours the Insured Person can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

(19) Territory means the countries in which cover applies, as shown in the schedule.
(20) Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with the Insured Person on the same trip.
(21) Trip means a journey that starts and ends in the Insured Person's home country during the policy period.
(22) Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

§ 2  Limits and excess
(1) Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(2) Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $25,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
(3) Trip Cancellation: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(4) Travel Delay: limit $750 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(5) The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

§ 3  Optional cover: Travel Delay
(1) The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
(2) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.
(3) The Insurer will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

§ 4  Currency
(1) All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
(2) Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

§ 5  Trip Cancellation
(1) The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
(2) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 7 days after the policy start date.
(3) The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
(4) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
(5) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

§ 6  Exchange of information
(1) To prevent fraud, the Insurer may check the details the Insured Person gives against public records and industry databases.
(2) The Insurer may contact previous insurers to confirm the Insured Person's claims history.

§ 7  Cooperation
(1) The Insured Person must give the Insurer all the help and information the Insurer reasonably need to settle a claim.
(2) The Insured Person must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Insurer's written permission.

§ 8  Geographical limits
(1) Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
(2) Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

§ 9  Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
(1) A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

§ 10  Emergency Medical Expenses
(1) The Insurer will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
(2) The most the Insurer will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $400 per incident.
(3) The most the Insurer will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $300 per incident.
(4) The Insurer will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
(5) The Insurer will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
(6) The Insurer will not pay for any claim arising from the Insured Person's being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

§ 11  Baggage and Personal Belongings
(1) The Insurer will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to the Insured Person's baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
(2) The most the Insurer will pay for Valuables under this section is $250 per incident.
(3) The most the Insurer will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $450 per incident.
(4) The Insurer will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
(5) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
(6) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

§ 12  Legal expenses abroad
(1) The Insurer will pay legal costs to pursue compensation for the Insured Person's injury or death caused by a third party during the trip.
(2) The Insurer will not pay legal costs unless the Insurer's legal adviser agrees that the claim has a reasonable prospect of success.

§ 13  Arbitration
(1) If the Insurer accepts a claim but disagree with the Insured Person about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
(2) Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against the Insurer.

§ 14  Records and evidence
(1) The Insured Person should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
(2) Where proof of value is missing, the Insurer may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
(3) The Insurer may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

§ 15  Sanctions
(1) The Insurer will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Insurer to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

§ 16  Emergency assistance
(1) The Insurer's emergency assistance service is available 24 hours a day on the number shown in the schedule.
(2) The Insured Person must contact the assistance service before being admitted to hospital as an in-patient, unless it is an emergency.
(3) The assistance service can arrange payment guarantees, interpreters and transport home.

§ 17  Reasonable precautions
(1) The Insured Person must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
(2) The Insured Person must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

§ 18  Communication
(1) The Insurer will communicate with the Insured Person in English.
(2) The Insurer may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

§ 19  Environmental commitment
(1) Where practical, the Insurer will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
(2) The Insured Person may ask for a new part instead, and the Insurer will tell the Insured Person whether any additional cost would apply.

§ 20  Notices
(1) Any notice the Insurer gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Insurer holds.
(2) Notices from the Insured Person should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

§ 21  Waiver
(1) If the Insurer does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Insurer has given up the right to enforce it later.

§ 22  Repatriation
(1) If the Insurer's medical adviser agrees it is necessary, the Insurer will arrange and pay for the Insured Person to be brought home.
(2) The Insurer will decide the method of transport and the time of repatriation after speaking to the treating doctor.

§ 23  Automatic renewal
(1) Unless the Insured Person tells the Insurer otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Insurer holds.
(2) The Insured Person can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Insurer's helpline.

§ 24  Severability
(1) If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

§ 25  Payment of claims
(1) The Insurer will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Insured Person's name.
(2) The Insurer aims to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents the Insurer needs.

§ 26  Interpretation
(1) Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
(2) Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
(3) Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

§ 27  Rental car excess
(1) If the Insured Person hires a car during the trip, the Insurer will reimburse any excess the Insured Person must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
(2) This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

§ 28  Third-party administrators
(1) The Insurer may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Insurer's behalf.
(2) Any company the Insurer appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

§ 29  Claims documents
(1) The Insured Person must provide, at the Insured Person's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Insurer reasonably ask for.
(2) The Insurer may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

§ 30  Inflation
(1) The Insurer may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
(2) Any adjustment will be shown in the Insured Person's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

§ 31  Joint policyholders
(1) Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
(2) A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

§ 32  Customer support
(1) The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
(2) Outside these hours the Insured Person can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

§ 33  Renewal
(1) The Insurer will write to the Insured Person at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
(2) The Insurer is not obliged to offer renewal.

§ 34  Governing law
(1) This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
(2) Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

§ 35  Other insurance
(1) If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Insurer will pay only the Insurer's proportionate share.
(2) The Insured Person must tell the Insurer about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Insured Person makes a claim.

§ 36  Accessibility
(1) This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

§ 37  Data protection
(1) The Insurer will use the personal information the Insured Person provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
(2) The Insurer will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
(3) The Insured Person can ask for a copy of the personal information the Insurer holds by writing to the Insurer's data protection officer.

§ 38  Missed departure
(1) The Insurer will pay reasonable additional travel and accommodation costs to reach the Insured Person's destination if the Insured Person arrives too late to board the Insured Person's booked transport because public transport fails.
(2) The Insured Person must allow enough time to reach the departure point, and must obtain written confirmation of the delay from the transport operator.

§ 39  Premium payment
(1) The Insured Person must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
(2) If an instalment is not paid within 21 days of its due date, the Insurer may cancel the policy after giving notice.

§ 40  Compensation scheme
(1) The Insurer is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
(2) If the Insurer cannot meet the Insurer's obligations, the Insured Person may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

§ 41  Personal liability
(1) The Insurer will pay damages the Insured Person becomes legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
(2) This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
(3) The most the Insurer will pay under this section is $5,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

§ 42  Assignment
(1) The Insured Person cannot transfer the Insured Person's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Insurer's written consent.

§ 43  Complaints
(1) If the Insured Person has a complaint, the Insured Person should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
(2) The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
(3) If the Insured Person remains dissatisfied, the Insured Person may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

§ 44  Salvage
(1) When the Insurer replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Insurer's property.
(2) If stolen property is recovered after the Insurer has paid a claim, the Insured Person must tell the Insurer and either return the payment or give the Insurer the property.

§ 45  Subrogation
(1) The Insurer will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Insured Person's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
(2) The Insurer can take action in the Insured Person's name to recover any payment the Insurer makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

§ 46  Duty of fair presentation
(1) The Insured Person must answer all questions the Insurer asks honestly and to the best of the Insured Person's knowledge.
(2) If the Insured Person gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Insurer may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
(3) If the Insured Person gives incorrect information carelessly, the Insurer may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

§ 47  Changes in circumstances
(1) The Insured Person must tell the Insurer as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
(2) The Insurer may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

§ 48  Fraud
(1) If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Insurer will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
(2) The Insurer may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

§ 49  Market conditions
(1) If the replacement item is no longer available, the Insurer will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

§ 50  Taxes
(1) The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
(2) If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

§ 51  General exclusions
(1) The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(2) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(3) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Insured Person.
(4) The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
(5) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

§ 52  How to read this document
(1) This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
(2) Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
(3) Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

§ 53  Interest
(1) The Insurer will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

§ 54  Electronic documents
(1) The Insurer will send documents by email unless the Insured Person asks for paper copies.
(2) The Insured Person must tell the Insurer if the Insured Person's email address changes.
(3) Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

§ 55  Discounts
(1) Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
(2) If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

§ 56  Recovery of costs
(1) If the Insurer pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Insurer may ask the Insured Person to repay the amount.

§ 57  Change of address
(1) The Insured Person must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Insured Person changes the Insured Person's address.
(2) The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

§ 58  Instalment agreements
(1) If the Insured Person pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
(2) Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

§ 59  Making a claim
(1) The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 30 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(2) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(3) The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

§ 60  Cancellation
(1) The Insured Person can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
(2) After the first 14 days the Insured Person can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $30.
(3) The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Insured Person 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

§ 6  Discounts

(2) If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

§ 7  Inflation
(1) The Insurer may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
(2) Any adjustment will be shown in the Policyholder's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

§ 8  Contents temporarily removed
(1) The Policyholder's contents are covered while temporarily removed from the home to another building in the same country, for up to 60 days.
(2) Contents in a student hall of residence are covered only if the student is a member of the Policyholder's family.

§ 9  Change of address
(1) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Policyholder changes the Policyholder's address.
(2) The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

§ 10  Cooperation

(2) The Policyholder must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Insurer's written permission.

(3) The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 30 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

(1) Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
(2) Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
(3) Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

§ 13  Alternative accommodation
(1) If the Policyholder's home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, the Insurer will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
(2) The Insurer will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with the Policyholder.
(3) Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

§ 14  How to read this document
(1) This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
(2) Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
(3) Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

ANNUAL MULTI-TRIP TRAVEL COVER
Issued by Compass Mutual
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Compass Mutual and "the Insured Person" means the person named in the schedule.

§ 1  Definitions
(1) Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
(2) Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
(3) Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
(4) Family means the Insured Person's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Insured Person.
(5) Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,000 metres.
(6) Limit means the most the Insurer will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
(7) Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
(8) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
(9) Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which the Insured Person received treatment or advice in the 12 months before the policy start date.
(10) Public transport means any scheduled train, bus, coach, ferry or aircraft.
(11) Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 12 hours.
(12) Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
(13) Territory means the countries in which cover applies, as shown in the schedule.
(14) Trip means a journey that starts and ends in the Insured Person's home country during the policy period.
(15) Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

§ 2  Limits and excess
(1) Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $75 per claim.
(2) Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
(3) Trip Cancellation: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(4) Travel Delay: limit $500 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
(5) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

§ 3  Optional cover: Travel Delay
(1) The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
(2) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.
(3) The Insurer will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

§ 4  Baggage and Personal Belongings
(1) The Insurer will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to the Insured Person's baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
(2) The most the Insurer will pay for Valuables under this section is $500 per incident.
(3) The most the Insurer will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.
(4) The Insurer will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
(5) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
(6) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

§ 5  Legal expenses abroad
(1) The Insurer will pay legal costs to pursue compensation for the Insured Person's injury or death caused by a third party during the trip.
(2) The Insurer will not pay legal costs unless the Insurer's legal adviser agrees that the claim has a reasonable prospect of success.

§ 6  Personal liability
(1) The Insurer will pay damages the Insured Person becomes legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
(2) This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
(3) The most the Insurer will pay under this section is $5,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

§ 7  Sanctions
(1) The Insurer will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Insurer to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

§ 8  Data protection
(1) The Insurer will use the personal information the Insured Person provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
(2) The Insurer will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
(3) The Insured Person can ask for a copy of the personal information the Insurer holds by writing to the Insurer's data protection officer.

§ 9  Communication
(1) The Insurer will communicate with the Insured Person in English.
(2) The Insurer may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

§ 10  Repatriation
(1) If the Insurer's medical adviser agrees it is necessary, the Insurer will arrange and pay for the Insured Person to be brought home.
(2) The Insurer will decide the method of transport and the time of repatriation after speaking to the treating doctor.

§ 11  Trip Cancellation
(1) The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
(2) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 7 days after the policy start date.
(3) The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
(4) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
(5) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

§ 12  Emergency Medical Expenses
(1) The Insurer will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
(2) The most the Insurer will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $400 per incident.
(3) The most the Insurer will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
(4) The Insurer will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
(5) The Insurer will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
(6) The Insurer will not pay for any claim arising from the Insured Person's being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

§ 13  How to read this document
(1) This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
(2) Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
(3) Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

§ 14  Changes in circumstances
(1) The Insured Person must tell the Insurer as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
(2) The Insurer may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

§ 15  Payment of claims
(1) The Insurer will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Insured Person's name.
(2) The Insurer aims to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents the Insurer needs.

§ 16  Recovery of costs
(1) If the Insurer pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Insurer may ask the Insured Person to repay the amount.

§ 17  Interest
(1) The Insurer will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

§ 18  Geographical limits
(1) Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
(2) Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

§ 19  Discounts
(1) Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
(2) If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

§ 20  Currency
(1) All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
(2) Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

§ 21  Premium payment
(1) The Insured Person must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
(2) If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, the Insurer may cancel the policy after giving notice.

§ 22  Interpretation
(1) Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
(2) Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
(3) Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

§ 23  Renewal
(1) The Insurer will write to the Insured Person at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
(2) The Insurer is not obliged to offer renewal.

§ 24  Records and evidence
(1) The Insured Person should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
(2) Where proof of value is missing, the Insurer may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
(3) The Insurer may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

§ 25  Notices
(1) Any notice the Insurer gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Insurer holds.
(2) Notices from the Insured Person should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

§ 26  Rental car excess
(1) If the Insured Person hires a car during the trip, the Insurer will reimburse any excess the Insured Person must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
(2) This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

§ 27  Exchange of information
(1) To prevent fraud, the Insurer may check the details the Insured Person gives against public records and industry databases.
(2) The Insurer may contact previous insurers to confirm the Insured Person's claims history.

§ 28  General exclusions
(1) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(2) The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
(3) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(4) The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
(5) The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(6) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Insured Person.

§ 29  Accessibility
(1) This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

§ 30  Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
(1) A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

§ 31  Making a claim
(1) The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 14 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(2) The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(3) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

§ 32  Instalment agreements
(1) If the Insured Person pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
(2) Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

§ 33  Joint policyholders
(1) Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
(2) A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

§ 34  Assignment
(1) The Insured Person cannot transfer the Insured Person's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Insurer's written consent.

§ 35  Taxes
(1) The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
(2) If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

§ 36  Environmental commitment
(1) Where practical, the Insurer will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
(2) The Insured Person may ask for a new part instead, and the Insurer will tell the Insured Person whether any additional cost would apply.

(2) Where proof of value is missing, the Insurer may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.

§ 12  Geographical limits

(1) The Insured Person must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
(2) The Insured Person must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

§ 14  Taxes
(1) The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
(2) If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

§ 15  Joint policyholders
(1) Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
(2) A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

(1) If the Insurer's medical adviser agrees it is necessary, the Insurer will arrange and pay for the Insured Person to be brought home.

(1) The Insurer will use the personal information the Insured Person provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.

(2) The Policyholder must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

§ 43  Discounts
(1) Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
(2) If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

§ 44  Claims documents
(1) The Policyholder must provide, at the Policyholder's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Insurer reasonably ask for.
(2) The Insurer may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

§ 45  Optional cover: Accidental Damage
(1) The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
(2) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
(3) The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $500 per incident.
(4) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
(5) The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

§ 46  Tenant's improvements
(1) If the Policyholder rents the home, the Insurer will pay for damage to fixtures and fittings that the Policyholder installed and are responsible for.
(2) This cover applies only to improvements the Policyholder paid for, not to items provided by the landlord.

§ 47  General exclusions
(1) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(2) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(3) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.
(4) The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(5) The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
(6) The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

§ 48  Sanctions
(1) The Insurer will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Insurer to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

§ 49  Duty of fair presentation
(1) The Policyholder must answer all questions the Insurer asks honestly and to the best of the Policyholder's knowledge.
(2) If the Policyholder gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Insurer may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
(3) If the Policyholder gives incorrect information carelessly, the Insurer may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

§ 50  Joint policyholders
(1) Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
(2) A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

§ 51  Customer support
(1) The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
(2) Outside these hours the Policyholder can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

§ 52  Interest
(1) The Insurer will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

§ 53  Making a claim
(1) The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(2) The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 14 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(3) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

§ 54  Freezer contents
(1) The Insurer will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.
(2) The Insurer will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

§ 55  Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
(1) A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

§ 56  Salvage
(1) When the Insurer replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Insurer's property.
(2) If stolen property is recovered after the Insurer has paid a claim, the Policyholder must tell the Insurer and either return the payment or give the Insurer the property.

§ 57  Locks and keys
(1) If the keys to the Policyholder's home are lost or stolen, the Insurer will pay the cost of replacing the locks to the outside doors.
(2) The most the Insurer will pay under this clause is $500 for any one claim.

§ 58  Notices
(1) Any notice the Insurer gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Insurer holds.
(2) Notices from the Policyholder should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

§ 59  Alternative accommodation
(1) If the Policyholder's home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, the Insurer will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
(2) The Insurer will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with the Policyholder.
(3) Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

§ 60  Currency
(1) All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
(2) Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

Issued by the Benefits Trust
In this policy, "the Plan" means the Benefits Trust and "the Member" means the person named in the schedule.

§ 1  Definitions
(1) Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
(2) Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
(3) Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
(4) Replacement period means 12 months from the date of the Member's last eyewear claim.
(5) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

§ 2  Limits and deductible
(1) Dental Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
(2) Vision Care: limit $500 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
(3) Therapy Services: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
(4) Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
(5) The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

§ 3  Vision Care
(1) The Plan will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
(2) The most the Plan will pay for Frames under this section is $120 per treatment.
(3) The Plan will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
(4) The Plan will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

§ 4  Dental Care
(1) The Plan will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
(2) No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
(3) The most the Plan will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $750 per treatment.
(4) The most the Plan will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $800 per treatment.
(5) The Plan will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
(6) The Plan will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

§ 5  General exclusions
(1) The Plan will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Plan from paying.
(2) The Plan will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(3) The Plan will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

§ 6  Making a claim
(1) The Member must notify the Plan of a claim within 14 days of the treatment. The Plan will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(2) The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(3) The Plan may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

§ 7  Joint policyholders
(1) Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
(2) A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

§ 8  Claims documents
(1) The Member must provide, at the Member's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Plan reasonably ask for.
(2) The Plan may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

§ 9  Assignment
(1) The Member cannot transfer the Member's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Plan's written consent.

§ 10  Sanctions
(1) The Plan will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Plan to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

§ 11  Leaving the plan
(1) Cover ends on the day the Member's employment ends or the day the Member stops being eligible, whichever is earlier.
(2) Claims for treatment received before cover ended may be submitted up to 90 days afterwards.

§ 12  Instalment agreements
(1) If the Member pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
(2) Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

§ 13  Recovery of costs
(1) If the Plan pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Plan may ask the Member to repay the amount.

§ 14  Fraud
(1) If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Plan will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
(2) The Plan may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

§ 15  Duty of fair presentation
(1) The Member must answer all questions the Plan asks honestly and to the best of the Member's knowledge.
(2) If the Member gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Plan may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
(3) If the Member gives incorrect information carelessly, the Plan may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

§ 16  Compensation scheme
(1) The Plan is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
(2) If the Plan cannot meet the Plan's obligations, the Member may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

§ 17  Reasonable precautions
(1) The Member must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
(2) The Member must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

§ 18  Eligibility
(1) Employees who work at least 20 hours a week are eligible to join the plan from their first day of employment.
(2) Contractors, agency workers and employees on unpaid leave of more than three months are not eligible.

§ 19  Wellness allowance
(1) Each plan year the Member may claim up to $100 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
(2) The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

In this policy, "the Insurer" means Hearthstone Insurance plc and "the Policyholder" means the person named in the schedule.

§ 1  Definitions
(1) Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
(2) Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
(3) Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to the Policyholder or the Policyholder's family.

(2) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by frost, storms, drought or animals.

§ 4  Taxes
(1) The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
(2) If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

§ 5  Third-party administrators
(1) The Insurer may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Insurer's behalf.
